adapters.mapping:
ACME Flame Design (PSI-10): normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames on porous burners aboard the ISS.

There are two tables, one for normal flames (fuel, diluted with N2, flows from the burner into an
oxygen-bearing chamber) and one for inverse flames (an O2 and N2 stream flows from the burner into an
ethylene-bearing chamber). Columns are mapped by hand, by exact header text.

Normal Flame table ("normal"):
- "Test" -> test_label, verbatim (for example "19115A1").
- "Fuel" -> fuel, verbatim ("C2H4" or "C3H8").
- "XO2 (init)" -> o2_pct (fraction_to_pct). The values run from 0.1980 to 0.4000, so they are mole fractions.
  In a normal flame the oxygen is in the chamber, and the header marks this as the initial value (a separate
  "XO2 (final)" column gives the value at the end of the test), so o2_basis is "chamber initial". "XO2
  (final)" is not mapped.
- "pmean (atm)" -> pressure_kpa (atm_to_kpa) and pressure_psi. The header states the unit as atm. On lines
  189 to 208 (day 13, C3H8) "pmean (atm)", "pfinal (atm)" and "XO2 (final)" are blank, so pressure_kpa is
  null there. "pinit (atm)" is recorded on those lines but is a different quantity and is never substituted;
  the gap is flagged missing_column with the lines listed.
- "Xfuel" -> fuel_conc_pct (fraction_to_pct): the fuel mole fraction of the burner stream (1 where "mN2
  (mg/s)" is 0). Where the cell reads "RAMPED" (lines 3, 5 and 7) or "RAMP" (57 rows) the value is null and
  each cell is flagged non_numeric; no value is inferred from neighbouring tests.
- outcome_label is not set: the table has no outcome column.
- Not mapped (kept in the raw columns): "Flame Type", "Day", "mfuel (mg/s)", "mN2 (mg/s)", "mtot (mg/s)",
  "XO2 (final)", "pinit (atm)", "pfinal (atm)", "mean Zst" and "Tad (K)". These also hold "RAMPED" or "RAMP"
  on the same rows; cells in columns that are not read are not parsed, so they raise no value flags.

Inverse Flame table ("inverse"):
- "Test" -> test_label, verbatim.
- "XO2" -> o2_pct (fraction_to_pct). The values run from 0.2120 to 0.8500, so they are mole fractions. In an
  inverse flame this is the oxygen fraction of the oxidiser stream leaving the burner (the table gives its
  mass flows "mO2 (mg/s)" and "mN2 (mg/s)"), so o2_basis is "oxidiser stream (inverse flame)". Where XO2
  reads "RAMP" (lines 31 to 33, 77, 78, 87, 88, 94 and 104) or "LOW O2" (lines 89 and 90) the value is null
  and the cell is flagged non_numeric.
- "pmean (atm)" -> pressure_kpa (atm_to_kpa) and pressure_psi.
- fuel is null ("not recorded") for this table and flagged missing_column. The table has no Fuel column, and
  the PSI page does not state which fuel the inverse flames used: its Objectives (ACME-Flame-Design.md lines
  25 to 27) name both C2H4 and CH4 for normal and inverse flames. The headers "XC2H4 initial" and "XC2H4
  final" point to C2H4 in the chamber, but a fuel is set as a per-table constant only when the PSI page
  states it, so no fuel is filled in here; readers can see those headers in the raw columns.
- fuel_conc_pct is null for this table. "XC2H4 initial" is the fuel mole fraction of the chamber ambient, not
  of a burner stream, and there is no canonical field that records which stream a fuel fraction belongs to,
  so it is left in the raw columns rather than mixed with burner-stream values from other tables.
- outcome_label is not set: the table has no outcome column.
- Line 87 has the test label "22042M1" among day 6 tests whose labels all begin "22024"; it is flagged
  label_inconsistent and kept verbatim.
- Not mapped (kept in the raw columns): "Flame Type", "Day", "mO2 (mg/s)", "mN2 (mg/s)", "mtot (mg/s)",
  "XC2H4 initial", "XC2H4 final", "pinit (atm)", "pfinal (atm)", "mean Zst" and "Tad (K)".

Both tables:
- Flow: the burner flows are recorded as mass flow rates in mg/s, not as velocities in cm/s, so flow_cm_s is
  null. The tables have no CO2, He, N2 percentage or flame-count column, and no calendar date.
- gravity_level is "microgravity (ISS)" from the PSI page (flight platform: International Space Station).
- PSI shows no licence for this investigation (ACME-Flame-Design.md line 19 is a dash); this is recorded as a
  no_licence flag.

ACME BRE (PSI-20): Burning Rate Emulator, a porous gas burner that emulates condensed-fuel burning.

Each row of the PSI table summarises one test day (a session of several flames), not a single flame.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Year", "Month" and "Date" -> test_date: the three cells joined with spaces exactly as written
  (for example "2019 Feb 8"). test_label is the same text with the prefix "Session ", because the
  table has no test number and each row is identified by its date.
- "Fuel Bottle" -> fuel, verbatim (for example "100% C2H4"). The fuel percentage inside this label is not
  read as a number, so fuel_conc_pct is null.
- "Oxygen Conc (percent)" -> o2_pct, read as a single percentage (an optional trailing '%' is removed).
  Most cells list several concentrations used during the session, separated by semicolons (for example
  "21; 26.5; 40"). A list is not one value and is not split, so these cells are flagged non_numeric and
  o2_pct is null; the raw cell is kept. Two cells read "3400%" (line 6) and "2100%" (line 9). Read as
  written they are 3400 and 2100 percent, which is outside the physical range, so they are flagged
  out_of_range and o2_pct is null. They are not reinterpreted as 34 or 21.
- o2_basis is "ambient" on every row with an oxygen cell: the table Notes (line 2) give the oxygen
  concentration "as diluted with nitrogen on a volume basis", the PSI page Objectives name "O2/N2 ambients"
  in "a quiescent microgravity ambient", and the PSI page Approach says the oxygen concentration is set as
  part of "the chamber contents". It is set even though every o2_pct is null, because it describes what
  the raw cell measures.
- "Flames Ignited" -> n_flames (the number ignited on that day, as the line 3 note says).
- "Burner Size (mm)" and "Notes" -> notes, as "Burner size (mm): 25; Notes: ...". The notes on lines 2 and
  3 are footnotes for the whole table, kept on the rows where they appear.
- diluent is "N2", a table constant from the line 2 note ("as diluted with nitrogen on a volume basis").
- Pressure: the table has no pressure column. The line 2 note says "The chamber pressures were also
  varied but are not identified in this summary table." pressure_kpa and pressure_psi are null. The
  pressures named on the PSI page are planned conditions, not values for any row, and are not used.
- Flow: the burner burned in a quiescent ambient; the table has no flow column, so flow_cm_s is null.

Checks: rows out of date order are flagged date_inconsistent (line 14, 2020 Dec 4, follows line 13,
2020 Dec 5). Fuel labels that differ only by spacing ("100%C2H4" against "100% C2H4") are flagged
label_inconsistent. Fuel labels are also checked for the fill-down pattern used in the other ACME tables.

ACME CLD Flame (PSI-21): coflow laminar diffusion flames of nitrogen-diluted methane and ethylene.

Each row of the PSI table summarises one test day (several flames), not a single flame.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Test Day" -> test_label and test_date, as text. The line 2 note says the value is the two-digit year
  followed by the three-digit day of the year (for example "17319"); it is not converted to a date.
- "Fuel Bottle" -> fuel, verbatim. 26 of the 32 labels carry spreadsheet fill-down errors (for example
  "40% CH5" to "40% CH14", "100% C2H5" to "100% C2H11"). Each affected cell is flagged fill_down_error and
  the label is kept exactly as written; no formula is corrected.
- "Fuel conc. Range" -> fuel_conc_pct, read as a single percentage. Most cells are ranges such as
  "30%-40%"; a range is not one value, so those cells are flagged non_numeric and fuel_conc_pct is null.
  Single values such as "40%" are read as written.
- "Flames ignited" -> n_flames (the number ignited on that test day, as the line 2 note says).
- "Test Type" and "Notes" -> notes, as "Test type: ...; Notes: ...". The note on line 2 is a footnote for
  the whole table, kept on the row where it appears.
- "Fuel MFC" and "N2 MFC" are the maximum flow rates of the mass flow controllers used (slpm on a
  nitrogen basis, line 2 note). They are equipment ranges, not flow velocities, so they are not mapped to
  flow_cm_s; they stay in the raw row.
- diluent is "N2" (the fuel diluent), a table constant from the line 2 note ("as diluted with nitrogen on
  a volume basis").
- Oxygen, pressure and flow: the table has no column for any of them, so o2_pct, pressure_kpa,
  pressure_psi and flow_cm_s are null.

ACME E-FIELD Flames (PSI-22): laminar diffusion flames of methane and ethylene under an electric field.

Each row of the PSI table summarises one test day (several flames), not a single flame.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Test Day" -> test_label, as text (YYDDD: two-digit year and day of the year in GMT, line 2 note).
- "Year", "Month" and "Date" -> test_date: the three cells joined with spaces exactly as written
  (for example "2018 3 14"). Each Test Day is checked against these cells; a mismatch would be flagged
  date_inconsistent (none is found).
- "Fuel Bottle" -> fuel, verbatim.
- "Fuel Conc" -> fuel_conc_pct, read as a single percentage (the trailing '%' is removed).
- "Flames Ignited" -> n_flames (the number ignited on that day, as the line 5 note says).
- "Test Type", "Mesh Polarity" and "Notes" -> notes, as "Test type: ...; Mesh polarity: ...; Notes: ...".
  The notes on lines 2 to 5 are footnotes for the whole table, kept on the rows where they appear.
- diluent is "N2" (the fuel diluent), a table constant from the line 4 note ("diluted with nitrogen on a
  volume basis").
- Oxygen, pressure and flow: the table has no column for any of them, so o2_pct, pressure_kpa,
  pressure_psi and flow_cm_s are null.

Continuation rows: some rows have an empty Test Type and carry only a Fuel Conc (for example
",,,,,,,100%,,"), apparently a further fuel concentration used on the test day above. They are kept as
test rows with only fuel_conc_pct (and, on line 4, notes) recorded. Nothing is filled down from the row
above, so their test day, fuel and flame count are null. Rows that are byte-identical to an earlier row are
removed automatically. Lines 30 to 33 repeat lines 26 to 29 (the 18319 test day), and the "100%" stubs
on lines 15, 19, 25, 29 and 33 are identical to the stub on line 7, so all eight are recorded as removed
copies (line 33 as a copy of line 7, its first occurrence). Because a stub carries no test day, an
identical stub under a different test day cannot be told apart from a repeat, so the automatic rule
applies; the removed lines are listed in the reconciliation.

ACME s-Flame (PSI-23): spherical diffusion flames from a porous spherical burner.

Each row of the PSI table summarises one test day (several flames), not a single flame. Fuel mixed with a
diluent issues from the spherical burner into an oxidising atmosphere, so the oxygen is the ambient.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Test Day*" -> test_label, as text (YYDDD: two-digit year and day of the year in GMT, line 2 note).
- "Year", "Month" and "Date" -> test_date: the three cells joined with spaces exactly as written
  (for example "2019 Sept. 11"). Each Test Day is checked against these cells; a mismatch would be flagged
  date_inconsistent (none is found).
- "Atmosphere*" -> o2_pct. Every cell is free text such as "~21% O2 with N2" or "~30% and ~21% O2 with He".
  An approximate percentage inside text is not read as a number, so each cell is flagged non_numeric and
  o2_pct is null. The text is kept in notes. o2_basis is "ambient" on every row with an Atmosphere cell.
- "Fuel Bottle" -> fuel, verbatim (for example "50% C2H4 with N2"). The fuel percentage inside the label is
  not read as a number, so fuel_conc_pct is null.
- Fill-down errors: "~21% O2 with N3" (lines 3 and 7), "N4" (lines 4 and 8), "N5" (line 9) and "N6"
  (line 10) in Atmosphere, and "50% C2H4 with N3" (line 3) and "45% CH4 with N3" (line 5) in Fuel Bottle,
  follow the row above with the final number increased by 1. Each cell is flagged fill_down_error and kept
  verbatim; no diluent is corrected.
- "Flames Ignited*" -> n_flames (the number ignited on that day, as the line 4 note says).
- "Test Type", "Atmosphere*" and "Notes" -> notes, as "Test type: ...; Atmosphere: ...; Notes: ...". The
  notes on lines 2 to 4 are footnotes for the whole table, kept on the rows where they appear.
- Pressure: the table has no pressure column. The line 3 note says the atmosphere is about 1 atm and that
  pressure rises with vitiation; that approximate statement is not used as a value, so pressure_kpa and
  pressure_psi are null.
- Flow: the table has no flow column, so flow_cm_s is null.
- diluent is not set: it differs between rows (nitrogen or helium) and is recorded only inside free text.

Checks: line 11 is labelled "First round of tests with nitrogen-diluted fuel and oxygen" while its
Atmosphere and Fuel Bottle both say "with He"; it is flagged implausible_value and kept as written. The PSI
page gives investigation dates of 02-05-2015 to 11-24-2019 (month-day-year), but 14 rows (lines 6 to 19,
from 2019 Dec. 18 onwards) are dated after that end date; they are listed in one metadata_inconsistent
flag, and both the row dates and the page dates are kept.

BASS-II (PSI-25): Burning and Suppression of Solids II, solid samples in a small wind tunnel on the ISS.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Test #" -> test_label (raw text, for example "B1" or "P22a")
- "Date" -> test_date (raw text, never reformatted)
- "Fuel Sample Material" -> material, verbatim (for example "1/4"" black rod" as PSI writes it)
- "Calibrated  initial O2 % by vol " -> o2_pct (percent, read as written). The header says this is the
  initial composition of the working volume, so o2_basis is "chamber initial". The PSI page says oxygen
  was varied below 21% by adding nitrogen, so diluent is the constant "N2".
- "Initial CO2 % by vol" -> co2_pct (percent, read as written)
- "Calibrated final O2 % by vol", "Final CO2 % by vol", "Initial CO (ppm)", "Final CO (ppm)" and
  "Total Frames Shot" are not canonical fields. They are kept in the raw record and only checked (below).
- "Fan display", "Air display" and "Flow restrictor" are instrument display settings written as free
  text sequences (for example "5   down to ext"). They are not velocities in cm/s, so flow_cm_s is null
  ('not recorded'). "Radiometer gain", "PI", "GMT" and "Sample #" are kept in the raw record only.
- pressure_kpa and pressure_psi are null: the table has no pressure column.
- gravity_level is the constant "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page (flight platform ISS, hardware MSG).

Every row is a test; none is excluded.

Checks (each one only adds a flag; no value is changed):
- implausible_value on "Calibrated final O2 % by vol" when the final O2 differs from the initial O2 of
  the same row by more than 5 percentage points. Burning in the closed working volume changes O2 by a
  few tenths to about 3 points in every other test, so a final value such as 1.6 or 40.4 cannot be the
  real final composition. On the split a/b rows (P22a/P22b, T28a/T28b) the values look shifted between
  columns; nothing is moved, and the initial O2 and initial CO2 on those rows are kept as written.
- implausible_value on "Initial CO2 % by vol" when it reads 0 while every other numeric initial CO2 in
  the table is above zero (line 15, B14: 0 against 0.19 to 1.85 elsewhere; the final O2, final CO2 and
  final CO on that row are "none"). The value 0 is kept as written.
- non_numeric on the non-canonical numeric columns above when a cell holds text such as "none", "video",
  "OR", "over", ">500" or "300+   +102". Blank cells are not flagged.
- date_inconsistent on "Date" when the date is not written as month/day/four-digit year, or when its
  year differs from the years of both neighbouring rows of the same PI (T9 and T18 are dated 2018 among
  2014 rows; their GMT day and sample numbers match the 6/24/2014 run of T10).
- date_inconsistent on "GMT" when the GMT day of year does not match the day of year of the written date
  (line 60, O10: GMT 213 against 7/22/2014, which is day 203).
- label_inconsistent for the misspellings "blac rod" and "2ide" in the material text.

BASS (PSI-26): Burning and Suppression of Solids, solid samples burned in a small flow duct on the ISS.

The PSI table has six columns only. It records which sample was burned and when, but no oxygen, pressure
or flow condition.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Test #" -> test_label (raw text, for example "12-R2" or "82a")
- "Date" -> test_date (raw text, never reformatted)
- "Fuel Sample Material" -> material, verbatim. The cell often carries a short remark after the material
  (for example "SIBAL 2 cm   opposed flow" or "2 cm sphere   wake ign"); it is kept as written.
- "GMT" (day of year), "As Run Test #" and "Sample #" are not canonical fields. They are kept in the raw
  record and used only for the checks below.
- o2_pct, pressure_kpa, pressure_psi and flow_cm_s are null ('not recorded'): the table has no column for
  them. The PSI page says the fan gave air flows of up to 40 cm/s, but no per-test flow is recorded.
- gravity_level is the constant "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page (flight platform ISS, hardware MSG).

Rows that are not tests: line 67 ("SOOT Cleaning", dated 8/3/2012, with no test or sample number) is a
hardware cleaning entry and is excluded. Every other row is kept.

Checks (each one only adds a flag; no value is changed):
- date_inconsistent on "Date" when the date is not written as month/day/four-digit year (line 44 reads
  "6/29/`12"), or when its year differs from the years of both neighbouring test rows (line 111 reads
  "5/15/2103" between two rows dated 2013).
- date_inconsistent on "GMT" when the GMT day of year does not match the day of year of the written date
  (line 100, and lines 118 to 123).
- near_duplicate on "As Run Test #" and on "Test #" when the same number appears on more than one row.
  All the rows are kept, because they differ in date, sample or material.
- label_inconsistent for the spellings "parrafin" (written "paraffin" elsewhere) and "oppsed".

CFI (PSI-39): Cool Flames Investigation, n-dodecane and n-dodecane/iso-dodecane droplets in the MDCA.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Flex Number" -> test_label. The first column of the CFI table is headed "Flex Number"; its values
  (1206 to 1387) are kept verbatim as the test label.
- "Test Date" -> test_date (raw text, for example "9-Mar-17").
- "Fuel " -> fuel (verbatim, for example "[.60]/[.40] C12H26/iso-dodecane").
- "Oxygen" -> o2_pct (fraction_to_pct). The header gives no unit; the values (0.17 and 0.21) sum with
  "Nitrogen" and "Helium" to about 1, so they are mole fractions, as in the sibling FLEX table.
  o2_basis is "ambient": the value is the MDCA chamber atmosphere around the droplet.
- "Nitrogen" -> n2_pct and "Helium" -> he_pct (fraction_to_pct, same reasoning).
- diluent: a text label from the recorded fractions, "N2" when helium is 0 and "N2 + He" when helium is
  above 0; null if either fraction is unknown. It describes the row and adds no new value.
- "Pressure" -> pressure_kpa and pressure_psi. The header has no unit, but every cell states its own unit,
  for example "1 atm" or "0.75 atm ". The allowed transform strip_stated_unit reads a number only when the
  unit written in the cell is exactly "atm"; any other cell is flagged non_numeric and left null. The raw
  pressure text is also kept in notes.
- "Local Time", "CIR " and "Fiber" have no canonical field; they stay in the raw record. They are used
  only for checks: the CIR code (for example "f068a03") carries the day of year, which is compared with
  "Test Date", and within one CIR day the local times are checked to run in CIR sequence order.
- gravity_level: "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page flight platform.
- outcome_label and flow are not recorded in this table.
- Byte-identical duplicates (lines 81 to 88 repeat lines 24 to 31) are removed by the framework.

DAFT / DAFT-2 (PSI-47): Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test, aerosol counter checks on the ISS.

DAFT tested particle counters with a dust aerosol; nothing was burned. The 2 rows are dust sampling
sessions. They are kept as records with fuel class "none" and test kind "dust", so they never mix with
fire evidence.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Session Name" -> test_label, verbatim ("D1", "D2").
- "Actual Day" -> test_date, verbatim (for example "GMT 54 (2005)").
- "Sample Material" -> material, verbatim ("Arizona Road Dust (ARD Fine) in combination with ISS GN2 ...").
  The PSI page Approach calls the same standard "Arizona Red Dust (ARD)"; the two names are kept as written
  and flagged label_inconsistent.
- "Hardware Description" -> notes, verbatim (which counter the session used).
- "Sampled Location" has no canonical field and stays in the raw record.
- o2_pct, pressure and flow: the table has no column for them, so they are null.
- gravity_level: "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page flight platform.

FLEX-2 (PSI-68): Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2, burning fuel droplets in the MDCA.

The FLEX-2 table on PSI is a test matrix, not a list of individual tests: each of its 8 rows names one
fuel and gives the ranges or lists of conditions used with it (for example O2 "0.17; 0.21;0.25; 0.3" and
pressure "0.5; 1.0; 1.5; 2.0; or 3.0"). Every row is kept as a record because each names a fuel that was
burned, but no single condition can be read from a list or a range without choosing one, so the numeric
fields are null and each such cell is flagged non_numeric.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Sample (Fuel Type)" -> fuel, verbatim (for example "Propanol (95%) Glycerol (5%) (mixture)").
  test_label uses the same column, as the table has no test number.
- "Ambient Gas Mixture " -> diluent, verbatim ("O2/N2 or O2/He").
- "Oxygen Mole Fraction" -> o2_pct (fraction_to_pct); o2_basis is "ambient", the chamber atmosphere.
- "Ambient Pressure (atm)" -> pressure_kpa (atm_to_kpa) and pressure_psi; the header states atm.
- "Flow Velocity (cm/s)" -> flow_cm_s; the header states cm/s.
- "Initial Droplet Diameter (mm)" and " Ambient Temperature (C)" have no canonical field and stay in the
  raw record.
- gravity_level: "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page flight platform.
- The table records no test date and no outcome.

FLEX (PSI-69): Flame Extinguishment Experiment, burning fuel droplets in the MDCA.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "FLEX Test #" and "FLEX Identifier" -> test_label ("<#> / <identifier>")
- "Test Date" -> test_date (raw text)
- "Fuel" -> fuel
- "Ambient pressure; mmHg" -> pressure_kpa (mmhg_to_kpa) and pressure_psi
- "O initial ambient composition; mole fraction" -> o2_pct (fraction_to_pct). The subscript 2 was lost
  from the PSI header; the column is O2.
- "N initial ..." -> n2_pct; "CO initial ..." (CO2, subscript lost) -> co2_pct; "He initial ..." -> he_pct
- "Test end" -> outcome_label, verbatim (Extinction, Disruption, Completion). "Disruption" is not defined on
  the PSI page and is never paraphrased.
- suppressant: derived label from which diluent is present ("CO2", "He", "CO2 + He" or "none"), using only the
  recorded fractions; it is a description of the row, not a new value.
- Flow: FLEX droplets burned in a quiescent chamber; the table has no flow column, so flow is null.

SAFFIRE-I (PSI-98): Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment I, a large SIBAL fabric sample burned in Cygnus.

The burns took place in the Saffire flow duct on the Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Sample Number " -> test_label (raw text, "S1" or "S2")
- "Material" -> material, verbatim ("SIBAL Fabric")
- "Percent O2" -> o2_pct (percent). The value is the oxygen in the cabin air drawn through the duct, so
  o2_basis is "ambient". Both cells are written as a range or an approximation ("21.5 - 21.7" and
  "~ 21.5"); no number is taken from such text, so both are flagged non_numeric and o2_pct is null.
- "Air Flow (cm/s)" -> flow_cm_s (the header states cm/s)
- "Flow Direction " -> notes, verbatim ("Concurrent" or "Opposed")
- pressure_kpa and pressure_psi are null: the table has no pressure column.
- gravity_level is the constant "microgravity (Cygnus)", from the PSI page Approach text. (The page's
  flight platform field says ISS, but the Approach and hardware fields say the burns ran in Cygnus.)
- Sample thickness, length and width, ignition power and time, burn time and the camera file names are
  not canonical fields; they are kept in the raw record.
- The table has no test date column, so test_date is not recorded.

Rows that are not tests: lines 4 and 5 ("F1C1/F1C2" and "F2C1/F2C2", "Pre-test flow visulation data for
sample 1" and "... sample 2") list flow-visualisation camera files recorded before the burns. They hold
no burn data and are excluded. Lines 2 and 3 are the two burns.

Checks (each one only adds a flag; no value is changed):
- swapped_columns on "Sample Length (cm)" and "Sample Width (cm)" when the length is shorter than the
  width. Lines 2 and 3 give length 40.6 and width 94. The SAFFIRE-I page Approach says the sample was
  about 0.94 m long and 0.4 m wide, and the SAFFIRE-III table gives length 94 cm and width 40.6 cm for
  the same SIBAL sample size. The values are kept as written; no swap is applied.
- unit_unclear on "Sample Thickness (cm)": 0.37 cm here and ".33 cm" in SAFFIRE-III, but SAFFIRE-II
  lists SIBAL as "037 mm", which cannot be read as a number and is in a different unit. The files do not
  settle which unit is right.

SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99): Spacecraft Fire Experiment II, nine 5 cm by 29 cm solid samples burned in Cygnus.

The burns took place in the Saffire flow duct on the Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Sample Number" -> test_label (raw text, "2-1" to "2-9")
- "Material" -> material, verbatim. The cell is blank on lines 7 (2-6) and 10 (2-9); material is then
  null ('not recorded') and the row is flagged. No material is copied from a neighbouring row.
- "Percent O2 (Note 1)" -> o2_pct (percent). Note 1 of the table (line 13) says the value is derived from
  measured CO2 production and referenced to the initial O2 reported by ISS: it describes the cabin air
  drawn through the duct, so o2_basis is "ambient". Every cell is written as an approximation or a range
  ("~ 22.1", "22.1 to 22.0"); no number is taken from such text, so each is flagged non_numeric and
  o2_pct is null.
- "Air Flow (cm/s)" -> flow_cm_s. Every cell repeats the unit ("20 cm/s"); the allowed transform
  strip_stated_unit reads the number because the unit written in the cell is exactly the header's cm/s.
- "Flow Direction" -> notes, verbatim ("Concurrent" or "Opposed")
- pressure_kpa and pressure_psi are null: the table has no pressure column.
- gravity_level is the constant "microgravity (Cygnus)", from the PSI page (flight platform Cygnus).
- Thickness, length, width, ignition, burn time, the low-gravity and 1-g burn and spread columns and the
  camera file names are not canonical fields; they are kept in the raw record.
- The table has no test date column, so test_date is not recorded.

Rows that are not tests: lines 11 and 12 ("Pre-test flow visulation data for sample 2-1" and "... 2-2")
list flow-visualisation camera files with no burn data; lines 13 to 16 are the table's Notes 1 to 4. All
six are excluded. Lines 2 to 10 are the nine burns.

Checks (each one only adds a flag; no value is changed):
- non_numeric on "Samle Thickness" for "037 mm" (lines 5 to 7): a number with a leading zero and no
  decimal point, so the intended thickness cannot be read from the cell.
- missing_column on "Material" for a blank material cell on a test row.
- label_inconsistent on "Camera 1" and "Camera 2" when a camera file name is blank or does not follow the
  pattern S<sample>C<camera> used on the other rows (line 4 Camera 1 blank, line 5 Camera 2 "S4C1",
  line 7 Camera 2 "S56C2"). "n/a" is accepted.
- label_inconsistent for header text: "Samle Thickness " (a typo for Sample) and "?-g Burn Length" and
  "?-g Spread Length", where the micro sign was lost and is a literal "?".

SAFFIRE-III (PSI-100): Spacecraft Fire Experiment III, a large SIBAL fabric sample burned in Cygnus.

The burns took place in the Saffire flow duct on the Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Sample Number " -> test_label (raw text, "S1" or "S2")
- "Material" -> material, verbatim ("SIBAL Fabric")
- "Air Flow " -> flow_cm_s. The header gives no unit but every cell states one ("30 cm/s"); the allowed
  transform strip_stated_unit reads the number only when the unit written in the cell is exactly cm/s.
  (The PSI page Approach gives 30 cm/s for SAFFIRE-III; that page value is not copied in.)
- "Direction" -> notes, verbatim ("Concurrent" or "Opposed")
- o2_pct is null: the table has no oxygen column.
- pressure_kpa and pressure_psi are null: the table has no pressure column.
- gravity_level is the constant "microgravity (Cygnus)", from the PSI page Approach text. (The page's
  flight platform field says ISS, but the Approach and hardware fields say the burns ran in Cygnus.)
- Sample thickness, length and width and the camera file names are not canonical fields; they are kept
  in the raw record.
- The table has no test date column, so test_date is not recorded.

Both rows (lines 2 and 3) are burns; none is excluded.

SAME-R (PSI-101): Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Reflight, smoke from overheated materials.

These are smoke tests: the samples were heated to produce smoke, not burned to a flame. Rows whose test
number ends in "a" (for example "51a", Description "aged") are a later measurement of the same smoke after
ageing; they are rows of the table and are kept as records.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "SAME Test #" -> test_label, verbatim.
- "Sample Type" -> material, verbatim (Kapton, Silicone, Lampwick, Teflon, Pyrell).
- "Date" -> test_date, verbatim (for example "21-Jul"). The dates have no year; the PSI page gives the flight
  tests as July 16 to September 9, 2010. No year is added.
- "Description" -> notes, verbatim.
- "Inlet velocity (cm/s)" -> flow_cm_s; the header states cm/s. A value of 0 is a recorded no-flow run.
- "Rt/R0", "Duration (sec)", "Primary aging time (sec)", "Primary mixing time (sec)" and "Net aging time
  (sec)" have no canonical field and stay in the raw record.
- Test 57 appears twice, as Lampwick (line 57) and as Teflon (line 75), with the same values in every other
  column. Both rows are kept and flagged near_duplicate.
- o2_pct and pressure: the table has no column for them, so they are null.
- gravity_level: "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page flight platform.

SAME (PSI-102): Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment, smoke from overheated spacecraft materials.

These are smoke tests: the samples were heated to produce smoke, not burned to a flame.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Sample #" -> test_label, verbatim.
- "Sample Material  " -> material, verbatim.
- "Air Flow (cm/s)" -> flow_cm_s; the header states cm/s.
- "Weight loss rate (mg/min)" and "Aging Duration (minutes)" have no canonical field and stay in the raw
  record.
- Lines 6 to 9 (samples 5 to 8) give only a material and the note "same conditions as 1-4", for example
  "Kapton: same conditions as 1-4", with the other cells empty. Each names a sample that was tested, so they
  are kept as test records. The material text is kept verbatim and the conditions of samples 1 to 4 are not
  copied into them, so their flow is null (not recorded).
- o2_pct and pressure: the table has no column for them, so they are null.
- gravity_level: "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page flight platform.

SLICE (PSI-106): Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment, gas jet flames in co-flowing air.

The SLICE table has only two columns, and each row is one day of testing, not one flame: the "Fuel Type"
cell often adds what else was run that day (for example "including 1 pyrometry calibration test").

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "Test Date" -> test_date, verbatim after trimming (for example "2012-FEB-09"). Several cells carry
  trailing prose after the date ("2012-FEB-13 SLICE testing with "); those cells are flagged
  date_inconsistent and kept as written.
- "Fuel Type" -> fuel, verbatim (for example "40% CH4 (balance N2) including 2 pyrometry calibration tests and
  2 fan calibrations"). No number is read out of this text; fuel_conc_pct is null.
- Line 13 reads "2012-MAR-23 Last day of testing: SPICE testing with 100% C3H8 and then 100%" with fuel
  "100% C2H4". It describes SPICE testing on the last day rather than a SLICE run. It is kept as a record,
  because it records a day of testing in this table and is not clearly a non-test row, and it is flagged
  implausible_value so it can be reviewed.
- o2_pct, pressure and flow: the table has no column for them, so they are null.
- gravity_level: "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page flight platform.

SPICE (PSI-107): Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment, gas jet flames in co-flowing air in the MSG.

Each row is one fuel flow setting of a flame; one ignition (same "GMT ignition" time) can have several rows
with different fuel rates.

Column mapping (written out by hand so it can be audited):
- "GMT ignition" -> test_label, verbatim (a clock time, or a marker such as "Ku LOS").
- "GMT date" -> test_date, verbatim. It holds the day of year only (45 to 174) with no year; the PSI page
  gives no investigation dates either.
- "Fuel" -> fuel, verbatim. Two spellings of one fuel occur ("75 % Propylene" and "75% Propylene"); both
  are kept as written and one label_inconsistent flag lists them.
- "Air Rate (cm/s)" -> flow_cm_s; the header states cm/s. It is the co-flow air velocity. Negative values
  (-0.28 and -5.92) are outside the physical range, flagged out_of_range and set to null. Blank cells are
  null.
- "GMT  Flame Off ", "Nozzle (mm)", "Fuel Rate (sccm)", "Fuel Rate (mg/s)" and "HC Fuel Rate (mg/s)" have no
  canonical field and stay in the raw record. The two GMT time columns are checked: times written with dots
  (for example "11.38.51"), or holding a marker instead of a time, are flagged date_inconsistent.
- o2_pct and pressure: the table has no oxygen or pressure column, so both are null.
- gravity_level: "microgravity (ISS)", from the PSI page flight platform.
- Byte-identical duplicates (34 extra copies) are removed by the framework.

ACME CFI-G (PSI-159): Cool Flames Investigation with Gases, spherical porous-burner flames on the ISS.

There are two tables, one for normal flames (fuel flows from the burner into an oxygen-bearing chamber) and
one for inverse flames (an oxygen stream flows from the burner into a fuel-bearing chamber). Columns are
mapped by hand, by exact header text.

Normal Flames table ("normal"):
- "Test" -> test_label, verbatim (for example "21088A1", "21088 B1"; the spacing varies and is kept).
- "Fuel" -> fuel, verbatim (for example "ethane", "50% butane", "30% propane").
- " XO2 before test" -> o2_pct (fraction_to_pct). The values run from 0.1797 to 0.3997, so they are mole
  fractions, not percentages. In a normal flame the oxygen is in the chamber, and this column gives the
  chamber value at the start of each test (within a run of tests, a test's "before" value usually equals the
  previous test's "XO2  after test"), so o2_basis is "chamber initial". The "after test" column is not mapped.
- "approx p (bar)" -> pressure_kpa (bar_to_kpa) and pressure_psi. The header states the unit as bar.
- "Xf" -> fuel_conc_pct (fraction_to_pct): the fuel mole fraction of the burner stream, written as a fraction
  (0 to 1). Lines 69 and 77 record Xf = 0 with mHC = 0, while the other tests of that series record Xf =
  0.02717, and the PI's derived Tad and Zst read "#DIV/0!" on those rows. The values are kept and the rows
  are flagged implausible_value for review.
- "Self-ext or flow term" -> outcome_label, verbatim ("SE", "FT" or "-"). A comment on line 5 reads "FC=flow
  cut", but the table does not define SE or FT, so they are never paraphrased. "-" appears where there was
  no ignition.
- "Comments" -> notes, verbatim.
- Not mapped (kept in the raw columns): "Flame Type", "Day" (a campaign day number, not a date), "Cool
  flame?", "XO2  after test", "mHC (mg/s)", "TFP", "Tad (K)" and "Zst" (quantities computed by the PI; lines
  69 and 77 hold "#DIV/0!" there), "Hot ignition", "burn time (sec)" and "Peak burner T (C )". Cells in
  columns that are not read are not parsed, so they raise no value flags.

Inverse Flames table ("inverse"):
- "Test" -> test_label; "Fuel" -> fuel (ethane, propane, butane), both verbatim.
- "XO2" -> o2_pct (fraction_to_pct). The values run from 0.12 to 0.85, so they are mole fractions. In an
  inverse flame this is the oxygen fraction of the oxidiser stream leaving the burner (the table also gives
  "O2 flow rate (mg/s)"), so o2_basis is "oxidiser stream (inverse flame)".
- "approx p (bar)" -> pressure_kpa (bar_to_kpa) and pressure_psi.
- "Self -ext or flow term" -> outcome_label, verbatim; "Comments" -> notes, verbatim.
- fuel_conc_pct is null for this table. "Xf  before test" is the fuel mole fraction of the chamber ambient,
  not of a burner stream, and there is no canonical field that records which stream a fuel fraction belongs
  to, so it is left in the raw columns rather than mixed with burner-stream values from other tables.
- Not mapped (kept in the raw columns): "Flame Type", "Day", "Xf  after test", "HC burnrate (mg/s)", "O2 flow
  rate (mg/s)", "TFP", "Tad (K)", "Zst", "Hot ignition", "burn time (sec)", "Peak burner Temp (C)", "Peak
  burner temp (K)" (lines 96 and 97 hold "#VALUE!"), and "Color".
- The file ends with 861 empty rows (lines 156 to 1016), which are excluded as blank rows.
- Label spellings that differ only in letter case ("Inverse" and "inverse" in Flame Type; "Yes" and "yes",
  "No" and "no" in Hot ignition; "Blue" and "blue", "Yellow" and "yellow" in Color) are flagged
  label_inconsistent and kept verbatim.

Both tables:
- Flow: the burner flows are recorded as mass flow rates in mg/s, not as velocities in cm/s, so flow_cm_s is
  null. The tables have no CO2, He, N2 or flame-count column, and no calendar date.
- gravity_level is "microgravity (ISS)" from the PSI page (flight platform: International Space Station).
- A test label whose leading day code differs from the other tests of the same Day would be flagged
  label_inconsistent; none do in these tables.
